summary: Intermittent 429s and throughput droops in dedicated pool during high churn of short-lived sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer NovaSearch reports intermittent 429 responses and sudden drop in throughput for their dedicated GPU pool during windows of high short-lived connection churn from their client fleet. Impact: user-facing request failures and p99 generation latency spikes; affects a production reserved pool serving search ranking-style prompts. Observed starting 2026-03-11 14:20 UTC and recurred in multiple short windows.

Background: NovaSearch uses many short-lived requests (median payload < 1s) from serverless worker fleet. Around the incident windows their client SDK rollout v2.4.5 increased connection shortness (keepalive=false), causing many ephemeral attaches and disconnects. Platform returned 429s and queued-fallbacks for a subset of routes that use large-batched quantized models.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a client fleet creating 10k short-lived HTTP/1.1 connections per minute (keepalive disabled).
2) Send lightweight inference payloads to dedicated pool pinned to customer pool config with model open-instruct-7B-quantized.
3) Observe attach latency metrics, number of ephemeral sessions, and autoscaler downscale events in the same window.
4) Confirm increased 429s at the API gateway and 'no available slots' errors in the serving runtime logs.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-12): customer traffic pattern changed after SDK rollout; high connection churn correlates with attach_latency and attach_failures spikes.
Telemetry: p50 latency for pool remained ~40ms but p95/p99 spiked to 600-1200ms during churn windows. Attach concurrency peaked and then dropped as autoscaler removed capacity mid-window.
Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler is reacting to transient load drops (many attaches that complete quickly) and downscaling aggressively, causing a brief capacity hole when the next surge arrives.

Hypothesis 2: 'Slot recycling' logic (releasing slots on short disconnects) combined with attach backoff introduces a serialization point on the allocator leading to API-level 429s even though aggregate GPU utilization is not saturated.

Experiment run (2026-03-13): reproduced in staging with synthetic short-lived-connections load; toggling autoscaler cooldown and increasing min_replicas prevented capacity hole and eliminated 429s in the test window.
Findings: Increasing min_replicas for this pool to maintain a small buffer removed API 429s; client-side keepalive dramatically reduced attach churn and resolved the root source.
comments: Ruth Allen (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported sudden 429 spike during traffic spike. Collected traces and asked for pool config and SDK version.
NovaSearch (Customer) 2026-03-12: Confirmed SDK 2.4.5 was rolled to 30% of fleet and can roll back; provided request samples and client connection patterns.

Tomás Rivera (SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced with load generator in staging. Autoscaler downscale_cooldown was too short for bursty ephemeral traffic; recommended increasing min_replicas and adjust churn detection thresholds.
Mei Chen (Platform Eng) 2026-03-13: Opened infra PR to add a bias window for downscale decision to ignore sub-2s bursts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1892

Tomás Rivera (SRE) 2026-03-14: Applied temporary workaround for NovaSearch: set pool.min_replicas=3 and autoscaler.downscale_cooldown=120s for their dedicated pool. Monitoring shows no further 429s in last 6 hours.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: increased dedicated pool min_replicas to 3 and set autoscaler downscale_cooldown to 120s for nova-dedicated-us-east. Customer rolled back SDK to v2.4.3 and re-enabled keepalive for workers as recommended which eliminated the attach churn. Engineering merged a tuning PR to add a short bias window to downscale decisions (see related_github_prs). Follow-up actions: schedule a permanent autoscaler tuning rollout, add a runbook entry recommending min_replicas or client-keepalive for high-churn workloads, and monitor for 72 hours. Ticket will be closed once monitoring confirms stability for 72h and customer confirms.
